title: Athletic Operator
author: Ian Sherer
desc:
Athletic Operator is the updated and expanded version of The Tactical Athlete, designed for military personnel, law enforcement officers, and other tactical professionals who need to be strong, powerful, and capable under physical stress.

Weekly Training Split

The program follows a four-day upper and lower body structure:

Day 1 – Lower + Back
Day 2 – Upper
Day 3 – Lower + Back + Grip
Day 4 – Upper

Each session is built around compound lifts, which form the foundation of the program. Sessions begin with explosive movements to develop power and improve force production. Accessory work supports the main lifts by addressing weak points and strengthening critical areas for tactical professionals, including the legs, back, shoulders, and trunk.

How the Program Works

The primary lifts follow structured percentage-based loading. This allows athletes to build strength progressively and consistently over time.

The program also incorporates structured jump progressions and throws throughout the training cycle to develop explosive power alongside strength and size.

During the foundation phase, accessory volume is higher to build muscle and reinforce movement quality. In the performance phase, accessory volume is reduced so the athlete can express strength and power without excessive fatigue.

Progression Structure

The program runs for 18 weeks and is divided into two phases with an extra week at the end for testing. 

Foundation Phase: Weeks 1–9

Intensity increases in three-week waves:

Weeks 1–3 @ 65% 1RM
Weeks 4–6 @ 70% 1RM
Weeks 7–9 @ 75% 1RM

Each main lift ends with a final AMRAP set to help drive progression.

Performance Phase: Weeks 10–18

Intensity continues to increase in three-week waves:

Weeks 10–12 @ 80% 1RM
Weeks 13–15 @ 85% 1RM
Weeks 16–18 @ 90% 1RM

Total training volume is gradually reduced to allow recovery and performance to rise. The focus shifts from accumulating work to expressing the strength and power developed throughout the foundation phase.

Auto-regulation Approach

Athletic Operator draws heavy inspiration from Alexander Bromley's Bullmastiff programming and Doug Young's auto-regulation methodology, while adapting its principles to better serve the demands of a tactical athlete.

The final set of each primary lift is performed as an AMRAP at the prescribed percentage. For every repetition completed above the target, 1% of the athlete's 1RM is added to the following week's working weight.

This allows the program to adjust to the athlete's actual performance and strength development rather than relying entirely on rigid percentages.
